title: Separate stellar velocity constants increase local mass errors in one TYC 9179-1083-1 orbit fit
abstract: We test separate constant stellar velocity shifts in a published joint orbit fit of TYC 9179-1083-1. A star-dependent constant plus an instrument constant gives masses of 0.808, 0.602 and 1.167 solar masses and mutual inclination 50.47 degrees. Four independent star and instrument constants remove both single GALAH velocities and both FEROS velocity means exactly. The local primary-mass error then rises from 0.069 to 0.248 solar masses; secondary and tertiary errors rise by factors of 3.3. An IAS15 refit gives 0.911, 0.643 and 1.238 solar masses, mutual angle 50.28 degrees and primary-mass error 0.247 solar masses. No constant shift is detected. Exact projection identities and derivative-step tests check the calculation. A linear planning test evaluates future two-star spectra under stable FEROS constants. No new observations are used. The result supports the tested local inclined geometry but limits its mass precision. Errors remain conditional on source weights, one bright-tertiary shape, one local prograde branch and constant shifts. Source measurements stay external; code, hashes, fitted states and aggregate evidence permit reproduction.

display.caption: Masses and mutual angles in the reference and calibration tests. Bars are local linear errors under the source weights.
Local primary-mass error after one simulated future two-star spectrum. The calculation assumes stable existing FEROS stellar constants and total error of 0.3 km/s for each future velocity.
